items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Out of all the singers I had told this to, only two really picked up on it and did it. One was Al Jarreau.

ctx.x: You sounded just like him at that point.

Yeah. He says, “I would like to be a jazz singer.” I said, “Oh. Why don’t you come up and sing something.” He says, “Oh, no, no, no, no. Not with you. Not with you.” I said, “Come on.” So I got him up, and he sang a tune. Then he asked me – he says, “How do you scat?” I’ve had people ask me that a lot. I had evolved my answer, which we talked about yesterday. I told him, “You know the melody.” He says, “Yeah.” I said, “Sing the chords.” Out of all the singers I had told this to, only two really picked up on it…
George could do it because he played. So he could do it anyway. But I’m talking about singers that didn’t know how to do it. George always could scat.
